residents.label: Ness County residents, July 1, 2025 (the trade area)

pop_trend.label: Population change per year from 2025
pop_trend.assumption: The county's estimate fell 2.4% between the April 2020 base and July 2025 [^1], roughly half a point a year, and the county reported zero residential building permits for 2025 [^1]. The model carries that pace forward; Year 1 is three years after the 2025 estimate, allowing for approvals and a build.

food_spend.label: Food-at-home spending per resident, 2025 dollars
food_spend.assumption: No food-at-home spending figure for Ness County is in the research. $2,700 is a round placeholder, a little under 6% of the county's per capita income of $45,085 [^1]. Against the county's 2022 retail sales of $4,528 per resident across all store types [^1] it is high, which is the reason to flag it: part of the county's food spending leaves the county and the placeholder may overstate what stays. A household survey or card-spend data should replace it.

food_inflation.label: Food price growth per year from 2025
food_inflation.assumption: An allowance; no Kansas food price series is in the research. The state's cut of its food sales tax to 0% on January 1, 2025 [^10] lowered shelf-plus-tax prices once and is not carried as a trend.

capture.label: Subject's share of county food-at-home spending
capture.assumption: A second full-line store must take share from an incumbent that belongs to a regional chain and offers online ordering [^11], and from the SNAP-authorized dollar stores [^12,23]. Part of the spend leaves the county as well. A quarter of the county's food spending by Year 3 assumes the new store becomes a real second choice for many households; no capture study exists, and the break-even table shows the share the loan would need.

deli_share.label: Deli and prepared food, share of store sales
deli_share.assumption: A small hot case and sandwich counter for school, hospital and oilfield lunch trade. No local sales split exists in the research.

grocery_gm.label: Gross margin on grocery, meat, produce and dairy
grocery_gm.assumption: The research holds no margin data for Kansas grocers. 24% is carried for one independent store buying through a wholesaler, without the purchasing scale of a chain incumbent [^11]; the lender should replace it with the wholesaler's quoted cost schedule.

deli_gm.label: Gross margin on deli and prepared food
deli_gm.assumption: Prepared food carries labor in its price, so its margin is higher than the aisle's; no benchmark is in the research.

payroll.label: Payroll, taxes and benefits (Year 1)
payroll.assumption: Matching an incumbent that stays open evenings and Sundays [^11] takes about eight full-time equivalents at a loaded cost near $34,000 each, including a manager, a meat cutter and deli staff. No Ness County wage figure is in the research; a county unemployment rate of 2.7% in 2024 [^4] points to a tight labor pool.

growth_payroll.label: Payroll growth per year
growth_payroll.assumption: An allowance for wages in a county with 2.7% unemployment [^4]; no local wage series is in the research.

utilities.label: Utilities (Year 1)
utilities.assumption: Refrigeration runs around the clock. The city operates a public water system under Chapter XV of its code [^8]; the electric and gas utilities and their rates were not found, so this is an allowance pending will-serve letters and rate schedules.

growth_utilities.label: Utility cost growth per year
growth_utilities.assumption: An allowance; no local rate history is in the research.

card_pct.label: Card and EBT processing, share of sales
card_pct.assumption: An allowance for card fees; SNAP purchases still run through EBT terminals at the dollar stores and the incumbent [^12,23]. No local benchmark.

supplies_pct.label: Supplies, repairs and maintenance, share of sales
supplies_pct.assumption: Bags, cleaning, case and compressor repairs. No benchmark is in the research.

admin_pct.label: Advertising, accounting, software and licences, share of sales
admin_pct.assumption: A weekly ad and digital coupons to answer the incumbent's online ordering [^11], plus accounting and the retail and food licences, which the research did not find. No benchmark.

insurance.label: Insurance (Year 1)
insurance.assumption: Property, spoilage, liability and workers' compensation. Wind, hail and flood conditions were not found in the research; a bound quote replaces this allowance.

growth_insurance.label: Insurance growth per year
growth_insurance.assumption: An allowance for premium increases on the High Plains; no local premium data.

reserve.label: Equipment replacement reserve (Year 1)
reserve.assumption: A few percent of the refrigeration and fixture budget a year, so compressors and cases can be replaced without new debt; no benchmark.

land_acres.label: Site area, acres
land_acres.assumption: A hypothetical pad of about two acres on the US 283 or K-96 frontage in Ness City [^5], enough for the building, parking and a truck dock. No particular parcel is assumed.

land_per_acre.label: Land price per acre
land_per_acre.assumption: The research holds no closed land sale and no assessed land value for Ness City, and no listing is used. $20,000 an acre is a round placeholder that an appraisal with closed sales must replace.

building_sf.label: Store size, square feet
building_sf.assumption: The smallest box that still carries a full fresh line (meat counter, produce, dairy, frozen and a deli) against a full-line incumbent. The incumbent's size was not found; the sales the county supports set the ceiling.

building_cost.label: Building cost per square foot
building_cost.assumption: A pre-engineered steel retail building with insulated panels and a refrigeration-ready slab. No construction cost index for the county is in the research; a contractor's estimate replaces it.

sitework.label: Site work, paving, utility taps and drainage
sitework.assumption: Parking, a truck dock, lighting, the city water tap under Chapter XV [^8] and a sewer connection whose provider is not confirmed. Connection fees were not found; this is an allowance.

equipment.label: Refrigeration, fixtures, meat room, deli and checkout
equipment.assumption: Walk-in coolers and freezers, display cases, shelving, meat-cutting and deli equipment, scales and point-of-sale with EBT. No benchmark is in the research; vendor quotes replace it.

contingency_pct.label: Hard-cost contingency
contingency_pct.assumption: Applied to building, site work and equipment for a store whose site, soils and utilities are not yet known.

soft_pct.label: Soft costs, share of building and site work
soft_pct.assumption: Design, engineering, permits, legal, the independent feasibility study and construction interest.

inventory.label: Opening inventory
inventory.assumption: About three weeks of Year 1 cost of goods. A wholesaler may take a lien on inventory, which the lender must settle in an intercreditor agreement.

working_capital.label: Pre-opening payroll and working capital
working_capital.assumption: Hiring and training before opening, grand-opening promotion and a cash cushion for the first months.

assess_ratio.label: Kansas assessment ratio, commercial real property
assess_ratio.assumption: The Kansas Constitution (Article 11) assesses commercial and industrial real property at a fixed share of value. The research prints no edition date for that text, so the share is carried here as an assumption, and the county appraiser confirms it [^9].

mill_levy.label: Ness County average mill levy, tax year 2025 (167.502 mills)

growth_tax.label: Property tax growth per year
growth_tax.assumption: An allowance for levy and value changes. The combined levy for the Ness City tax unit was not found; the county average is the substitute [^6,24].

bi_fee_pct.label: USDA guarantee fee, share of the guaranteed amount: 3.0% initial plus 0.50% for a guarantee issued before construction is complete (the terms sheet prints no base)

bi_annual_fee.label: USDA annual retention fee, share of guaranteed balance (the terms sheet prints no base)

usda_fee_paydown.label: Retention fee base decline per year
usda_fee_paydown.assumption: The retention fee is charged on the outstanding guaranteed balance; the model lowers the base by 3.5% of the original balance a year to approximate a 20-year amortization, a labelled simplification.

bi_rate.label: Interest rate
bi_rate.assumption: B&I rates are negotiated between lender and borrower, fixed, variable or combined [^17]. Prime was 7.00% on October 9, 2026 [^26]. The model carries Prime plus 1.00 point for a start-up store with no operating history; the lender sets the rate at pricing.

bi_amort_years.label: Amortization
bi_amort_years.assumption: USDA allows the useful life of the project or collateral, up to 40 years or the state-statute limit [^17]. Refrigeration and fixtures are about a third of the hard cost and wear out well before the building, so the model blends to 20 years.

bi_equity_min_pct.label: Minimum equity
bi_equity_min_pct.assumption: Not a USDA B&I rule: the USDA terms sheet in the research prints no equity percentage for B&I. For a new business with no operating history the study tests 25% of project cost, a lender-style figure under the credit evaluation described in 7 CFR 5001.202 [^18]; the lender's credit memo sets the real requirement.

bi_dscr_floor.label: Coverage floor
bi_dscr_floor.assumption: Not a USDA B&I rule: the USDA terms sheet prints no coverage ratio for B&I; the lender's credit policy governs. The study tests 1.25x in Year 3, the first year at a stable share, because the regulation asks for projections through at least two years at stable operations [^16].

uses.label: Site work, paving and utility taps
Soft costs, study and construction interest
uses.basis: share of building and site work

revenue.label: Grocery, meat, produce and dairy
revenue.expr: residents * (1 + pop_trend) ** (y + 3) * food_spend * (1 + food_inflation) ** (y + 3) * capture * (1 - deli_share)

revenue.label: Deli and prepared food
revenue.expr: residents * (1 + pop_trend) ** (y + 3) * food_spend * (1 + food_inflation) ** (y + 3) * capture * deli_share

opex.label: Property tax
opex.expr: (land_acres * land_per_acre + (building_sf * building_cost + sitework) * (1 + contingency_pct)) * assess_ratio * mill_levy * (1 + growth_tax) ** y

opex.label: USDA annual retention fee (passed through)
opex.expr: tpc * (1 - bi_equity_min_pct) * bi_guarantee_pct * bi_annual_fee * (1 - usda_fee_paydown * y)

proposed.note: the sponsor proposes the 25% equity this study assumes and a 20-year USDA-guaranteed loan for the balance

glance: Ness City, the seat of Ness County, Kansas, at the junction of US 283 and K-96 [^5]
